title: The OD Dashboard
subtitle: Four stages, fourteen steps. Every step shows what to have in hand, what to send, and what to get back, together with the honest build-status of each item.

chips.small: Pilot rate · Rapid Org Diagnostic · first FIVE engagements only
Advance / on completion — tie tranche 2 to handover, not the report

gate_banner: Before any intervention is designed (Stage III · Step 10), the engagement's specific problem gets an outside-expert check — matched to the right field, the right geography, the right scale. The design decision stays Rahul's; the client never sees the step. Skip only when the practice has already delivered and evidenced the same intervention in a comparable organisation, and name exactly which conditions the new case satisfies -- resemblance is not precedent.
sources_line: Everything an OD engagement needs lives inside this app: the process, the tasks, the documents, the client records. Client data syncs to your private GitHub repo; every change is recoverable from its history.

stages.title: Pre-Planning
stages.desc: Source on evidence, not signal. Qualify against real entry criteria. First touch and the follow-up clock.
stages.intro: The gate that already works. A funding announcement is a signal, not a qualification — the 8-org batch of 26 July was archived unsent for exactly this. Two organisations sourced under the current gate produced one draft, and that was the gate working.

steps.title: Before you contact anyone
have: A pipeline record created before any outreach
ClickUp Pre-Planning List: existing comms model · active members · their issue · their ask · terms
send: Nothing. No price, no pilot language, no claim about what is wrong with them.
get: A qualified name — or a recorded reason it was held (Akshaya Patra pattern)

rules.d: Real pain point · leadership willing to engage honestly · staff access possible · evidence reviewable · open to phased improvement. Fail any → no Touch-1 draft.

qa.q: They were just announced as a grant winner — good lead?
qa.a: A signal only. Run the fit-check. The 26-July batch of 8 was sourced from one grant announcement and archived unsent; signal-only sourcing is the recorded failure mode.

steps.title: First touch — the email
have: Real address from their own site or publication — never broker data (ZoomInfo, RocketReach)
Every claim re-sourced to the original document that morning (the SAFE grant claim failed exactly here)
VSS reference in permitted written form only: “an NGO managing multi-year institutional grant funding” — the ₹3cr figure never in writing
send: Touch-1 draft: under 90 words · one specific verifiable thing about THEM · no compliment sandwich · ask for a conversation, not a sale · “Dear [Name],” · no em dash
Attach nothing. Not the process note, not a profile, not a rate.
get: A reply — or silence, which starts the clock

rules.d: The email invites a conversation about what might be true. If they reply “that area is going fine”, that is a real answer, not a failed pitch — the hypothesis-testing email is the model.

qa.q: Can I mention the pilot rate to get attention?
qa.a: Never. Price never appears in the first email (the pricing rules). Sequence: conversation → scope → number.

steps.title: No reply — the follow-up clock
have: The schedule: T2 day 5 LinkedIn DM · T3 day 12 pure value · T4 day 20 soft close
Hard stop: no named contact → no draft, ever. Nothing addressed to a “Team”.
What “pure value” at Touch 3 actually is — undefined. Candidate: the NGO readiness self-check, once it ships
send: T2 short DM referencing the email
T3 one useful thing they can use whether or not they hire you
T4 soft close — door left open, clock stops
get: A reply at any touch, or a clean move to nurture — no chasing beyond T4

qa.q: They opened but never replied — send a 5th touch?
qa.a: No. After T4 the prospect moves to nurture. No-reply is the normal outcome, not a failure; working the schedule beats clever persistence.

steps.title: They reply
have: A holding reply + scheduling note. Two paragraphs and a calendar slot — smallest gap in the whole map
send: Warm confirmation within 24h: thank them, propose two time slots for a 20-minute call, promise nothing else

qa.q: Should I attach the process note now, before the call?
qa.a: No — before the call it is a brochure. Its moment is within 24 hours AFTER the call, when it answers “what happens next”.

stages.title: Conversion
stages.desc: The four moments where money and trust change hands. Strongest instincts, thinnest paperwork.
stages.intro: Your own methodology names this the first sale: — the first sale is not the service, it is trust in the diagnostic process. ClickUp already holds the call checklist and the 50/50 terms; the proposal and ToR templates do not exist yet.

steps.title: The 20-minute scoping call
have: Seven discovery questions: what is not working · who is affected · since when · what evidence · what was tried · what would improvement look like in daily work · who must approve change
ClickUp call structure: existing comms model · active members · their issue (5 types) · their ask
Rehearsed answer to “how will you actually do this?” — look before you fix → small adoptable set → tested with real users → handed over. Ends on the VSS monthly-review evidence
Note-capture format (the engagement brief is built from this call)
Disqualification script — criteria say when to walk away, nothing says how
send: Nothing in writing during the call. Never a number.
Within 24h AFTER: the OD Process Note (EN / HI-EN) — ⚠️ fill the five xxx placeholders first: For, Date, timeline, reference engagement, contact
get: Answers to all 7 questions, in their words — you will quote these back in the proposal
Their issue vs their shopping list — the distance between them is the diagnosis

rules.t: Item 3 vs item 5 — keep them apart
rules.d: “What issue do they want to solve” and “what do they think they need” are different answers. An org that names ‘no role clarity’ and asks for ‘report writing’ has just told you something it did not mean to.
“What have you already tried and stopped?” — the graveyard question. Three abandoned registers means the constraint is not format quality, and delivering a fourth is malpractice.

qa.q: All 7 questions + rapport + my own pitch in 20 minutes?
qa.a: It does not fit — that is the open gap. Priority order: their issue (Q1–Q4) → who approves → your one-paragraph how. Park the rest for the proposal call-back.

qa.q: They ask the price on the call?
qa.a: “I price by scope, not by hour — you'll have a number in the proposal within 48 hours of this call, tied to exactly what we agree here.” Never improvise a figure live.

steps.src: Step 4 · the methodology–1.4 · ClickUp Pre-Planning List

steps.title: The proposal
have: Proposal template — does not exist in any form. Largest single gap in the package
send: Their problem in THEIR words from the call · scope in/out · the phases with what they receive (Process Note) · what you need from them · timeline 2–3 weeks · THE NUMBER: ₹45,000 pilot shown against the ₹75,000–1,20,000 standard · the exchange: written case study + nameable reference, stated not implied · FCRA line if applicable
get: A yes, a negotiation, or a documented no

rules.t: Say five is bounded, in writing
rules.d: “First five engagements” goes in the proposal so the client understands the rate expires by design — that is what keeps a pilot rate from becoming the standing rate.
“Happy to align the contract structure with your FCRA auditor's guidance.” Nothing further, ever -- the auditor makes the legal call, never you.

qa.q: They ask for a discount on the pilot rate?
qa.a: Scope down, not price down (the pricing rules). Remove a module and keep the number honest — a discount at the door anchors permanently and NGO directors talk to each other.

steps.title: They confirm — the contract / ToR
have: Payment structure exists (ClickUp): 50% advance · 50% on completion
⚠️ Move tranche 2 off “report shared” onto handover-with-named-owner — else the contract pays for a document while says success is behaviour change (trigger text truncated; verify)
ToR template — promised as the Phase-1 deliverable in the Process Note, does not exist
Confidentiality clause · access clause · exit terms
send: ToR: parties · scope in/out · phases & dates · deliverables · what THEY provide · confidentiality both ways · fee & triggers · IP and case-study consent · access failure terms · exit
get: Signature + 50% advance + a named focal point
Case-study consent IN the contract — the pilot rate is traded for a written case study and a nameable reference; if it is not written here, you discounted for nothing

qa.q: They sign but the advance doesn't arrive?
qa.a: The engagement has not started. Kickoff is gated on signature AND advance — that is what the 50% is for.

steps.src: Step 6 · ClickUp item 4 · the pricing rules

stages.title: Delivery
stages.desc: Diagnosis first, always. One phase is fully proven (Implementation — VSS). One carries the CLARITY gate.
stages.intro: the methodology: every engagement starts with diagnosis, not solution design. Phase 5 is the one complete stage — six adopted policies at a delivered engagement prove it. Phase 2 is the weakest and most exposed: a scored capacity baseline is promised in writing and cannot yet be produced.

steps.title: Kickoff — intake & scoping
have: Signed ToR + advance received + named focal point
Engagement brief — the entry-criteria gate structures it from your notes; no template exists
send: The brief, for their validation: issue · affected functions · objective · stakeholders · time frame · constraints · expected outcome
get: 3–5 success indicators, set NOW, before anything changes (validation cycle Step 3). Skip this and Phase 6 has nothing to measure — this is where the evaluation problem is actually created

BASELINE: three countable things, same conversation, no instrument needed — how long X takes now · how many people touch it · where it stalls. one delivered engagement never got one -- and a case study with no baseline is an assertion, not proof (Clarity, highest-value change)

qa.q: What does a 3-countable baseline look like for a documentation problem?
qa.a: e.g. days from field visit to report reaching the office · number of hands it passes through · how many of last quarter's reports the funder returned with queries. Two hours of asking, written down before you touch anything.

steps.src: Step 7 · validation cycle Steps 3–4 · the adoption-judgment brief

steps.title: Diagnosis
have: Eight evidence sources · phase-2 method list · the hypothesis rule: thin evidence = hypothesis, never conclusion
the NGO readiness self-check — frames what to look at; NOT a baseline (self-scored, 10 min, pre-client)
Interview guide (prospect questions exist, diagnosis questions do not)

Capacity assessment instrument + scoring — adapt Marguerite Casey OCAT (free, spreadsheet, 4 domains) → Google Forms. The standing rule: never build a rival diagnostic to SELL; building one to deliver with is a different act
Observation protocol · interviewee confidentiality note (staff are about to tell you what is wrong with their own management)
Ten questions audited in from the Ingentis org-design checklist (14 Aug 2026), NGO-filtered — see the full ten below and the rules box for what was deliberately left out
get: Evidence from ≥3 sources · the existing registers (attendance notebook, WhatsApp group — the formats that already work) · the graveyard (tools started and stopped) · who is paid to do what, from which budget head

rules.d: VSS's own OD baseline: 12 areas · 37 sub-areas · 225 questions · 66.70%. That instrument already exists inside your one client's world.
What language will each document live in, and what language does its user work in? A finance policy in English for a Hindi-working accounts assistant is decoration with a signature.

rules.t: Ten diagnostic questions added from an external checklist (Ingentis org.manager, audited 2026-08-14)
rules.d: Meetings are goal-oriented and efficiently run · the org was designed deliberately or grew as patchwork · roles are measured by output/results, not just task/input · decision structure is efficient and involves the right people · there is a real internal leadership pipeline, not just a founder · managers have TIME and resources to mentor, not just the skill to · information silos or ‘expertise empires’ exist and are named · task-loads are realistic, not chronically overloaded · staff have real voice and influence, not just a title · knowledge is retained across staff turnover, not lost with each departure. Each closes a real gap this stage didn't cover — see engagement-runbook / package-review cross-check, audited 2026-08-14. Deliberately NOT imported: compensation streamlining and back-office sizing (both assume a corporate pay/HR scale most 5–30-staff Indian NGOs don't have — the real problem here is usually under-staffing, already covered by the budget-line test above) and any 'customer' framing (translate to donor/beneficiary/community, never paste the word itself into a client-facing document).

qa.q: Leadership offers to answer for everyone — skip staff interviews?
qa.a: No. Staff access is an entry criterion. If access fails now, the diagnosis is undeliverable — surface it as a contract issue, not a scheduling one.

steps.title: Feedback session
steps.tag: Phase 3 — trust is earned or lost here
have: five tests per recommendation: evidenced · feasible · mission-aligned · prioritised by impact/effort · plain language
Blame-direction rule (the writing style rules): every short declarative points AT the reader or at their expense — a diagnostic is read by the people whose work it describes
Plain-language test: would someone outside the sector understand every sentence on first read?
Diagnostic report template · facilitation plan · a method for “priorities agreed together” · what to do when leadership disagrees with a finding
send: The diagnostic report — evidence, assumptions and priority issues, each labelled; hypotheses marked as hypotheses
get: Agreed priorities, in writing, signed by whoever must approve change

qa.q: The director rejects a finding flat out?
qa.a: Ask what evidence would change their mind, then go get it or drop it. A finding held against the client's will dies at implementation anyway — 's adoption test starts in this room.

steps.title: Action planning — CLARITY GATE
steps.tag: Phase 4 · design only what they can adopt
have: ⚑ CLARITY runs BEFORE anything is designed. Feed it three things or it routes on a guess: the root-cause statement · the client's words for what they want built · what they tried and abandoned
CDC SMART checklist (in the folder): one action verb, nothing unmeasurable
The five issue types (ClickUp) map onto the menu: mis-communication → comms routines · role clarity → role clarification · workflow → redesign
Action plan + roadmap template · impact-vs-effort grid
send: Action design note: each intervention with what it REPLACES, who does it instead of what, on which day, and its forcing function
get: Client sign-off on a plan small enough to actually happen

rules.t: The adoption test, per item (Clarity verdict)
rules.d: Adoption capacity is not a score — it is a per-item prediction: what does this replace · who does it instead of what · on which day · what happens OUTSIDE the org if it is not done. No answer to “instead of what” = a practice added to somebody's evening.

rules.t: Which meeting does this live in?
rules.d: A design constraint, not a closing question. Any new practice lands on an existing recurring slot or it has no heartbeat — the one mechanism with real delivered-engagement evidence, and it writes most of the handover pack for free.

Sort every requested item by “who asked for this?” — auditor / FCRA / funder-format items get adopted; internal-virtue items get adopted last or never. Strongest predictor available, costs one question.

qa.q: When may the CLARITY gate be skipped?
qa.a: Only when the practice has already delivered and evidenced the SAME intervention in a comparable organisation — and then name exactly which conditions the new case satisfies. Resemblance is not precedent.

qa.q: The client insists on all four shopping-list items?
qa.a: Sort by forcing function in front of them: who asked for each, and what breaks externally if it isn't done. The list usually sorts itself; you never have to be the one saying no.

steps.src: methodology Phase 4 (Clarity standing step) · the adoption-judgment brief Parts 1–3

steps.title: Implementation
have: PROVEN AT VSS: six policies adopted org-wide (digital · finance · fundraising · gender · HR · vehicle) + operational formats + project timelines + proposal flow + first standardised comms infrastructure incl. website
The adoption test: can a real user understand it, use it, explain it, apply it — all four, in front of you
Are the six VSS policies filed as reusable templates? Possibly the most valuable unfiled asset in the practice — CHECK before building anything new
send: The smallest usable version, built WITH them — plain language, tested against field staff as the readers who matter
get: A real user passing the four-part adoption test · named owner per system

qa.q: They ask for two more policies mid-build?
qa.a: Boundary rule : if the core problem is unclear, pause and diagnose. Scope-adds go into a note for engagement two — that is also how a pilot client becomes a full-rate client.

steps.title: Evaluation
have: Validation cycle Steps 5–6 · : success = behaviour change, not deliverable count
Endline = the Step-8 instrument re-run; no instrument, no endline
Default indicator set · adoption-measurement method for: used? by whom? how often? what friction?
send: Evaluation note: each indicator against its Step-7 baseline
get: The case-study evidence the pilot rate paid for — numbers a funder can read

rules.t: The luck that must become method
rules.d: VSS making documentation a standing monthly agenda item was found by reading their LinkedIn four months later. A +90-day calendar entry per engagement turns the strongest evidence the practice owns from accident into procedure.

qa.q: Nothing measurably changed by evaluation time?
qa.a: Report it. Step 8 of the validation cycle: record what failed and which assumptions were wrong — do not scale what is not adopted. An honest null in the lesson log beats an inflated case study everywhere it matters.

steps.title: Exit & handover
steps.tag: Phase 7–8 · they stop needing you, on purpose
have: Transfer list (Phase 8): documented ownership · governance routines · training notes · editable templates · version control · review calendar
Versioning rule : every tool carries number, purpose, owner, review date
Handover pack template · ownership matrix · review-calendar template
send: The handover pack — largely written already if “which meeting does this live in” was answered at Step 10
get: ASK NOW, while goodwill is current: the written case study · the nameable reference (draft it for them) · written permission for what may be said, figures vs facts · one photo/artefact. This is what ₹45,000 of discount purchased — and tranche 2 should release here

qa.q: When exactly do I ask for the case study?
qa.a: At handover, same meeting, not months later. Draft the reference yourself and offer it for editing — a busy director approves a good draft and never writes one from scratch.

stages.title: After & Learn
stages.desc: The lesson log, the +90-day check, the pilot counter. What turns five engagements into a practice instead of five separate jobs.
stages.intro: the methodology is blunt: knowledge that is hard to find does not count as knowledge management. One engagement has produced one case note; at five pilots the cost of not running this layer is rebuilding the same things five times.

steps.title: Close the loop
have: Lesson log: context · issue · intervention · evidence used · adoption barriers · results · ASSUMPTIONS THAT PROVED WRONG · next time
Template library — file every reusable artefact with versioning, starting with the VSS six
Diagnostic pattern file — the ClickUp issue taxonomy is its beginning; add one row per engagement
send: Nothing outward — this step is for the practice
get: Reusable assets so engagement N+1 starts at 60%, not zero

rules.d: A pilot slot used is a pilot slot gone. Track n/5 — the moment engagement five closes, the rate is ₹75,000+ unless a fresh decision says otherwise.

qa.q: What goes in “assumptions that proved wrong”?
qa.a: The private version: what you believed about what they needed, what they would adopt, and how long it would take — against what happened. Clarity's note: by engagement four this file is worth more than the case studies.

steps.title: The 90-day check
have: A scheduled +30 and +90-day check-in per closed engagement — currently nothing fires
send: One short message to the named owner: “is it still being used?”
get: Adoption evidence as method, not luck — and often the second engagement: the check-in that finds a new problem is the warmest sourcing channel the practice has

qa.q: What if the answer is “we stopped using it”?
qa.a: Gold, twice over. It goes in the withdrawn-style lesson log (recorded failures do not repeat), and “what made it stop?” is a diagnostic conversation — which is Phase 1 of the next engagement.
